| '''Audience'''

|-

<span id="the-picture"></span>
== The picture ==

<pre> your notes ──awbrain harvest──▶ linked-Markdown wiki
                                        │  (top-k pages only)
 Discord ◀──slash commands──▶ awdiscord ──▶ agent (OpenAI-compatible endpoint)
                                   │
                          operators approve risky actions</pre>
Everything runs on your machine and your model. No vendor cloud sits in the middle, which is the point of the [[Company Brain/Memory and knowledge|aw family]].

<span id="before-you-start"></span>
== Before you start ==

* Python 3.10 or later
* A model server on the same machine: Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM or LM Studio. [[Company Brain/awdiscord#Setup|awdiscord setup]] finds it for you.
* A Discord account that can create an application
* A folder of Markdown notes or session exports

<span id="step-1-build-the-brain"></span>
== Step 1 — Build the brain ==

<syntaxhighlight lang="bash">pip install awbrain
awbrain harvest ~/notes
awbrain ask "what did we decide about the pool?"
awbrain verify "a self-owned platform beats a subscription computer"</syntaxhighlight>
<code>harvest</code> writes a wiki of pages joined by <code><nowiki>[[wikilinks]]</nowiki></code>; every claim is pinned to the file and line it came from. <code>ask</code> answers from the top-k pages only, never your whole history. Full commands: [[Company Brain/adk and awbrain command reference#awbrain|CLI reference]].

<span id="step-2-create-the-discord-application"></span>
== Step 2 — Create the Discord application ==

Discord does not allow this step from an API, so do it by hand:

# Open https://discord.com/developers/applications and create an application.
# Open '''Bot''' and press '''Reset Token'''. Copy the token; you paste it once in step 3.

<span id="step-3-install-and-run-the-bot"></span>
== Step 3 — Install and run the bot ==

<syntaxhighlight lang="bash">pip install "awdiscord[gateway]"
awdiscord setup     # paste the token; it does the rest
awdiscord run</syntaxhighlight>
<code>setup</code> checks it is a bot token, finds your model server, makes you the operator, saves settings to <code>~/.awdiscord/awdiscord.env</code> (mode 600), registers the slash commands and prints the install link. Open the link to add the bot to your server. See [[Company Brain/Safety rails|Safety rails]] for what permissions it asks for (four, and no more).

<span id="step-4-connect-the-brain-to-the-bot-design-proposal"></span>
== Step 4 — Connect the brain to the bot ''(design proposal)'' ==

<blockquote>'''Not verified.''' Neither README documents this link. Two plausible routes, to be tested:

# Run an <code>adk serve</code> agent whose tool calls <code>awbrain ask</code>, and point <code>AWDISCORD_AGENT_URL</code> at it.
# Write an [[Company Brain/Plugins and packs|awdiscord plugin]] whose command shells out to <code>awbrain ask</code> and posts the cited answer.

Either way, <code>/ask</code> or a new <code>/brain</code> command would return an answer with <code><nowiki>[[citation]]</nowiki></code> markers. This is the page a friendly vendor could fill in with the supported route.
</blockquote>
<span id="step-5-what-staff-can-now-do"></span>
== Step 5 — What staff can now do ==

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Command
! What it does
|-
| <code>/ask question</code>
| The agent answers. Add <code>private</code> to show only you
|-
| <code>/share</code>
| Post your last answer to the channel
|-
| <code>/faq ask</code>
| Answer from a curated FAQ only
|-
| <code>/task add</code> and <code>/standup</code>
| Track work; the agent writes a standup from the board
|-
| <code>/poll</code>
| Quick votes with buttons
|-
| <code>/status</code>
| Is the agent up, which personas exist
|}

Operators also get [[Company Brain/Approvals|Approve/Deny cards]] for risky actions. Full list: [[Company Brain/Discord command reference|Discord command reference]].

<span id="voice-calls"></span>
=== Voice calls ===

With voice enabled, the bot joins a voice channel, takes notes when someone says “Aither, take notes”, and posts a summary and action items at the end. Items that would spend money, delete data or publish outside the organisation are marked '''needs a decision, not done'''.

<span id="keeping-the-brain-fresh"></span>
== Keeping the brain fresh ==

<syntaxhighlight lang="bash">awbrain watch ~/notes     # re-harvests changed sources
awbrain status            # receipts: sources, pages, claims, embedder mode</syntaxhighlight>
